messages.content: Printer A takes 4 hours, printer B takes 12. How long together?

<think>
[frame: pathway=s2|mode=solve|construct=logic|persona=neutral|identity=none|theme=none|channel=reasoning]
Rates: 1/4 + 1/12. Common denominator 12: 3/12 + 1/12 = 4/12 = 1/3 stack per hour. Time is 3 hours. Averaging 4 and 12 to get 8 ignores that the fast printer does more of the work.
</think>

3 hours.
Why does WHERE LOWER(email) = 'a@b.c' ignore an index on email?

<think>
[frame: pathway=s2|mode=build|construct=ai_engineer|persona=neutral|identity=none|theme=none|channel=reasoning]
The index is sorted by the raw email bytes. LOWER(email) produces a different value, so that order can't be walked. The planner scans. An index on LOWER(email) would match the predicate. Comparing the raw column would use the existing index and would miss other casings.
</think>

The index is sorted by the raw email. LOWER(email) is a different value, so the planner can't walk that order. Index the expression if you need the case-insensitive match.

I know lists. Teach me, in one picture, what a dict does when two keys share a bucket.

<think>
[frame: pathway=s2|mode=teach|construct=teacher|persona=neutral|identity=none|theme=none|channel=reasoning]
They have the list. A dict is a row of boxes. The hash picks the box. Two keys in one box sit in a short chain, and lookup walks that chain with equality. Hash picks the box. Equality picks the key.
</think>

A dict is a row of boxes. The hash picks the box. If two keys share one, lookup walks the short chain in that box and checks equality. Hash chooses the box. Equality chooses the key.
Drills don't come back to the tool library. Three different fixes, then pick.

<think>
[frame: pathway=s2|mode=brainstorm|construct=brainstorm|persona=neutral|identity=none|theme=none|channel=reasoning]
Reminder texts are what already failed. A public list shames the people who read it. A deposit or card hold changes the cost of keeping the drill. Pick the hold. Cash deposit if they have no card. Same mechanism.
</think>

Pick a card hold, released on return. Reminders and a public late list don't change the cost of keeping the drill. No card, then a cash deposit.
